subject: Docs ownership handback + canary slot scheduling for Q1 rollout
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>; Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmecloud.com>
Cc: AtlasDocs Support <support@atlasdocs.io>
Date: Mon, 11 Dec 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Docs ownership handback + canary slot scheduling for Q1 rollout

Team —

I want to lock a short plan for docs ownership and a preliminary canary timetable for the January Q1 rollout we committed to Acme Cloud. High level asks:

- Marcus: can you confirm the runtime / config notes are final for the public docs? I have a couple of product-ask clarifications (see below).
- Lauren: need a single owner for the step-by-step enablement checklist and a deadline (we should be able to hand off to CS by 01/10).
- Tessa: ops — please propose two discrete canary slots (one low-traffic pre-cutover, one limited cohort post-cutover) and the rollback signal set.
- Vivek: product — confirm the doc copy for the new feature flags and any exceptions we expect to call out.

Sarah / AtlasDocs — thanks for standing by on the DocuSign and the extended formatting support. Im looping AtlasDocs in to confirm the attachment types well accept for the published docs.

I attached a very rough canary_slots_v1.xlsx and a first-pass enablement_faq_draft.md. Please reply with concrete owners / dates by EOD Wednesday PST so I can assemble the enablement playbook.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: canary_slots_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), enablement_faq_draft.md (markdown stub)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmecloud.com>, AtlasDocs Support <support@atlasdocs.io>
Date: Mon, 11 Dec 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Docs ownership handback + canary slot scheduling for Q1 rollout

Kimberly —

Quick status: runtime / config notes are functionally complete from engineerings side. I pushed the latest snippets to the docs drive (see link) and added a "known exceptions" section for the following:

- Feature flag behavior when KV cache warmup fails (graceful fallback to LRU policy).
- Quantization fallback (when we detect suboptimal perf on older GPUs).

I can own the runtime snippets and the exceptions section; target to have final copy by 12/15 so Lauren has a week to fold into the enablement checklist.

Two asks for product: Vivek, can you confirm whether we want to call out the "soft-deprecation" window for the legacy endpoint in the public notes, or keep that internal-only? That changes the language and the customer-facing rollback instructions.

—Marcus
Lead Engineer, Runtime

Date: Mon, 11 Dec 2028 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Docs ownership handback + canary slot scheduling for Q1 rollout

Thanks for the clear asks, Kim. I can own the enablement checklist and the step-by-step playbook. Proposed schedule:

- 12/20: Draft enablement checklist complete (internal review)
- 12/28: Incorporate engineering snippets + exceptions (Marcus)
- 01/05: CS training runbook & recorded walkthrough
- 01/10: Handoff to CS with assets on Drive + CS playbook

I'll set up a short triage slot next Wednesday (12/13 10:00-10:30 PT) to walk through open wording decisions — public vs internal phrasing, and the legacy endpoint note Marcus called out.

Also tagging product: Vivek, if we want the legacy endpoint note public, Ill need the exact phrasing (one paragraph) by EOD 12/15.

—Lauren
Manager, Enablement

Date: Tue, 12 Dec 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Docs ownership handback + canary slot scheduling for Q1 rollout

Looping in ops details. Proposed canary windows (subject to availability):

1) Pre-cutover low-traffic: 2029-01-08 02:00-04:00 PT (global low-traffic window) — scope: subset of Acme internal test tenants (~5%) on canary runtime.
2) Post-cutover limited cohort: 2029-01-15 18:00-22:00 PT — scope: limited customer cohort (by account tag).

Rollback/monitoring signals (high level):
- Error rate > 0.7% sustained for 5 minutes (API 5xx + model timeouts)
- Token latency p95 > 1.8x baseline for 10 minutes
- Quality regression alert triggered by the eval-run (automated prompt set)

I will prepare a short runbook stub and add it to the Drive folder by EOD 12/12. If AtlasDocs needs a specific file format for the public playbook export, tell us; otherwise well hand off a single PDF + source markdown.

—Tessa
Ops Lead, Platform Reliability

Subject: Re: Docs ownership handback + canary slot scheduling for Q1 rollout

Thanks all. Quick note on the legacy endpoint language: please keep deprecation language out of the public docs for now — well provide migration guidance but not a public timeline. Suggested public phrasing (single paragraph):

"If you are using legacy endpoints, we recommend transitioning to the new /v2/runtime endpoint. For migration steps and compatibility notes, contact your account team; we will provide migration guidance and support during your transition."

I can own the compatibility paragraph and will post an approved snippet by 12/15. Marcuss exceptions section can remain in the internal appendix.

—Vivek
VP, Product

Great progress, everyone — thanks for the quick turn. Short next steps (Ill own the action tracker):

- Marcus: finalize runtime snippets + internal exceptions by 12/15 (deliver to Drive).
- Lauren: lock triage slot 12/13 10:00-10:30 PT and update checklist draft by 12/20.
- Tessa: publish runbook stub + canary slot confirmation (Ill update playbook when you drop the runbook).
- Vivek: post approved migration paragraph by 12/15 (internal copy for appendix + public snippet withheld).
- Sarah / AtlasDocs: confirm acceptable file exports for public docs by 12/14.

Ill assemble the enablement playbook and send a single handoff package to CS on 01/10 assuming we hit these checkpoints. If any of the owners foresee slippage, ping me immediately so we can re-scope.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
